content: The old library stood at the end of the street, its walls covered in creeping plants. Inside, shelves of books reached to the ceiling, and the smell of old paper filled the air. Mr. Okafor, the librarian, knew every book by heart and could find any title in minutes. Children came after school to read and do their homework, and on rainy days the library was full. Though the building was old, it was the heart of learning in the town, and everyone agreed it must be protected.

content: The river was the lifeblood of the village. Women fetched water from it at dawn, children swam in its shallow parts, and fishermen cast their nets at dusk. When the rains came, the river swelled and flooded the farms near its banks, leaving rich soil behind. The elders warned the young ones never to swim in the deep part, where the current was strong. Yet the river was loved by all, for it gave the village water, fish and fertile land.
